Each table row (1-24) corresponds to one inspected object/equipment type; "indicator" holds the inspection-activity name (column "Наименование вида инспекции") and "object" holds the object/subarea (column "Область инспекции (подобласть)/стадия инспекции"). The "Код ОК" and "Код ТН ВЭД ЕАЭС" columns are filled with a dash placeholder (⸻) on every row of this document, so okpd2_code/tnved_code are null throughout. norm_doc is the requirements-documents column ("Документы, устанавливающие требования к объектам инспекции"), algorithmically segmented into individual documents joined with '; ' by a regex heuristic (looking for known document-type openers); segmentation is occasionally imprecise on long compound titles, so the exact original text (including the separate methods-documents column, "Документы, устанавливающие методы инспекции") is preserved verbatim in raw_row_text. Row 1 is unusually long (spans pages 1-20) as it lists the full base regulatory set for Электроустановка/эксплуатация; later rows for other equipment types largely restate an overlapping subset of the same documents, which is a genuine feature of the source, not a transcription error. Row numbering in the source itself skips no numbers (rows 1-24 all present); row 22 uses a different inspection-activity name ("Оценка соблюдения обязательных требований") than the other rows. Page 95 (the last page, PDF rotation 270°) is a scanned image with no extractable text layer; its two remaining requirements-document entries and the signature block were transcribed manually from the rendered page image and appended to row 24's norm_doc/raw_row_text. All other pages (1-94) contain a native text layer that was extracted programmatically (verified against the rendered page images for structure, rotation and column layout) rather than read via OCR/vision line-by-line, given the page count (95) and the highly repetitive boilerplate content.
